prerequisites: Knowledge of (492) Materials Science, including machinability and weldability of steels, heat treatments, stainless steels, tool steels, thermoplastic, thermosetting and elastomeric polymers, and non-destructive testing.
Knowledge of (495) Strength of Materials, specifically relationships between stresses and strains.
Knowledge of (839) Graphic Expression and CAD, including concepts of Computer-Aided Design, 2D and 3D representation, and dimensioning.
Knowledge of (845) Environmental Engineering, including basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand Manufacturing Engineering, as well as manufacturing systems and processes, and their place in the productive context.
Characterize the different elements of manufacturing processes.
Identify different processes, as well as their characteristics, for establishing classifications and systematic studies.
Understand machine tools, tools, and fixtures of the main manufacturing processes.
Acquire skills for the design, planning, and evaluation of manufacturing processes.
Understand the basics of Metrology and the application of metrological techniques in manufacturing.
Understand different welding processes, as well as the equipment and consumables used in welded joints.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to manufacturing processes - Definitions - An overview of manufacturing processes - Attributes of a manufacturing process - The importance of manufacturing - Influencing factors and challenges - Stages in product design and manufacturing
Introduction to Dimensional Metrology - Definitions - Tolerances and fit systems

Additive Manufacturing - Definitions, history, and current and future state - Applications of Additive Manufacturing - Additive Manufacturing Technologies. Promoting adhesion: special surfaces, chemicals, plasma surface treatments, etc. - CAE simulation in Additive Manufacturing - Comparison with other manufacturing processes

Material Removal Forming - Definitions and history of machining - Machining by chip removal - Definitions, materials, historical evolution of machines, applications, advantages and disadvantages, cutting tool, machine tool. - Turning: definition, operations, basic parameters, parts of a cutting insert, chip formation, machining angles, cutting mechanisms, cutting forces. - Tool materials, tool wear, surface finish (turning), optimal cutting parameters (turning), chip shape, insert geometries, insert identification, material machinability. - Milling: definition, climb milling and conventional milling, operations, cutting parameters. - Machining economics - Non-conventional machining (chemical, electrochemical, EDM, ultrasound, water jet, laser, plasma) - Comparison with other manufacturing processes

Molding - Plastic injection molding - Definitions. Global data. Environmental problems. Applications. Most used plastics. Overmolding. Gas-assisted injection. - Stages of the injection process. Injection cycle. The injection machine. The injection mold. - Polymers and their behavior when injected. Injection process parameters. Process window. - Typical defects and how to avoid them. Design recommendations for parts and molds. Simulation of the injection process. - Comparison with other manufacturing processes - Casting - Definitions and uses of casting. - Applications and most used metals. - Types of casting processes - Basic scheme of a poured casting - Casting process design and simulation software - Solidification time - Typical defects - Possible adverse health effects - Comparison with other manufacturing processes

Joining Processes - Welding, bolted joints, adhesives, plasma treatments (to promote adhesion or reduce friction) - Welding symbology - Weldability, welding defects - OAW flame welding - SMAW welding - TIG welding - MIG/MAG welding - SAW welding - Electric resistance welding. - Laser welding - Ultrasonic welding - Plasma welding
Plastic Deformation Forming - Definitions and materials - Rolling - Forging - Extrusion - Drawing - Cutting and punching - Bending and curving - Deep drawing and stamping
Machining by chip removal: Machining parts using semi-automatic lathe and milling machine and CNC milling machine.
Welding: Welding will be performed with different technologies.
Molding: Plastic injection molding will be done in a metal mold and in a 3D printed mold. Aluminum casting will be done in a sand mold.
Social project: Throughout the semester, a functional product will be developed to help people in need, using the different manufacturing processes studied in the subject.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must achieve a minimum score of 50% in Practical GL activities, written exams, individual activities, and presentations. Additionally, a minimum score of 50% must be obtained in each of the final tests: practical, presentation, project, and written exam. If any critical criterion is not met, the overall course grade will be a Fail, with the final score capped at a maximum of 4.5 points.
